hints: Use right-triangle trigonometry in $\triangle OPT$ to express $PT$ and $OT$ in terms of $r$ and $\alpha$.
Find $QT = OT - r$ and arc length $PQ = r\alpha$.
walkthrough:
Find the lengths of tangent $PT$ and hypotenuse $OT$ in the right-angled triangle $OPT$:
$$PT = r\tan\alpha$$
$$OT = \frac{r}{\cos\alpha}$$

Express the segment length $QT$ and the circular arc length $PQ$:
$$QT = OT - OQ = \frac{r}{\cos\alpha} - r$$
$$\text{Arc } PQ = r\alpha$$

Sum the three boundary lengths to obtain the perimeter of region $PQT$:
$$\text{Perimeter} = PT + QT + \text{Arc } PQ = r\tan\alpha + \left(\frac{r}{\cos\alpha} - r\right) + r\alpha = r\left(\tan\alpha + \frac{1}{\cos\alpha} - 1 + \alpha\right)$$

hints: Calculate the area of $\triangle OPT$ using $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2}(10)(10\tan\frac{\pi}{3})$.
Calculate the area of sector $OPQ$ using $\frac{1}{2}r^2\alpha = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)(\frac{\pi}{3})$.
Subtract the sector area from the triangle area.
walkthrough:
Calculate the area of the right-angled triangle $OPT$ with $r = 10$ and $\alpha = \frac{\pi}{3}$:
$$\text{Area of } \triangle OPT = \frac{1}{2} \times r \times r\tan\alpha = \frac{1}{2}(10)\left(10\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\right) = 50\sqrt{3} \approx 86.60$$

Calculate the area of the sector $OPQ$:
$$\text{Area of sector } OPQ = \frac{1}{2} r^2 \alpha = \frac{1}{2}(10^2)\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right) = \frac{50\pi}{3} \approx 52.36$$

Subtract the sector area from the triangle area to find the shaded area:
$$\text{Shaded Area} = 50\sqrt{3} - \frac{50\pi}{3} \approx 86.60 - 52.36 = 34.24 \approx 34\text{ (to 2 s.f.)}$$
